items.ko: 논리적으로 일관된
items.ex: A coherent paragraph has ideas that connect smoothly.
items.exko: 논리적으로 일관된 단락은 생각이 매끄럽게 이어져요.

items.ko: 자세히 설명하다
items.ex: Could you elaborate on your second point?
items.exko: 두 번째 요점을 더 자세히 설명해 주시겠어요?

items.ko: 반박하다
items.ex: She used two statistics to rebut his claim.
items.exko: 그녀는 두 개의 통계로 그의 주장을 반박했어요.

items.good: She enjoys hiking, swimming, and reading.
items.ko: 그녀는 하이킹, 수영, 독서를 즐겨요.
bad: She enjoys hiking, swimming, and to read.
She enjoys to hike, swimming, and reading.
She enjoys hiking, to swim, and reading.

cz.st: She enjoys hiking, swimming, and ___.

items.rule: 나열하는 항목은 같은 형태로 맞춰요(병렬 구조). enjoy 뒤에는 동명사가 와요.
items.hint: 나열된 항목의 형태가 서로 같은지 보세요.

items.good: The test was difficult; however, most students passed.
items.ko: 시험은 어려웠지만 대부분의 학생이 통과했어요.
bad: The test was difficult, but however most students passed.
The test was difficult; however, most students has passed.
The test was difficult; however, passed most students.

cz.st: The test was difficult; ___, most students passed.

items.rule: 두 개의 독립된 문장은 쉼표만으로 잇지 않아요(콤마 스플라이스). 세미콜론 뒤의 접속부사 다음에는 쉼표를 써요.

items.good: Opening the box, she found a letter.
items.ko: 상자를 열었을 때 그녀는 편지를 발견했어요.
bad: Opening the box, a letter was found.
Opening the box, the letter surprised her.
Opened the box, she found a letter.

cz.st: ___ the box, she found a letter.

items.rule: 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어와 같아야 해요. 상자를 연 사람은 she예요.
items.hint: 분사구문의 행위를 하는 사람이 누구인지 생각해 보세요.

items.good: The list of required books is posted on the door.
items.ko: 필수 도서 목록이 문에 붙어 있어요.
bad: The list of required books are posted on the door.
The list of required book is posted on the door.
The list of required books were posted on the door.

cz.st: The list of required books ___ posted on the door.

items.rule: 수식어구 속 명사가 아니라 핵심 주어(list)에 동사를 일치시켜요.

items.good: This secret is just between you and me.
items.ko: 이 비밀은 너와 나 사이에만 있어요.
bad: This secret is just between you and I.
This secret is just between you and mine.
This secret is just between your and me.

cz.st: This secret is just between you and ___.

items.rule: 전치사 뒤에는 목적격 대명사를 써요.

items.good: By the time we got to the cinema, the film had already started.
items.ko: 우리가 영화관에 도착했을 때 영화는 이미 시작했어요.
bad: By the time we got to the cinema, the film has already started.
By the time we got to the cinema, the film had already starting.
By the time we got to the cinema, the film is already started.

cz.st: By the time we got to the cinema, the film ___ already started.

items.rule: 과거의 한 시점보다 앞서 일어난 일은 과거완료(had + p.p.)로 나타내요.

items.good: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
items.ko: 내가 더 열심히 공부했다면 시험에 합격했을 거예요.
bad: If I would have studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I have studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would had passed the exam.

cz.st: If I had studied harder, I ___ have passed the exam.

items.rule: 과거 사실의 반대는 If + had p.p., would have p.p.로 나타내요.

items.good: The author whose book won the prize will visit our school.
items.ko: 그 책으로 상을 받은 작가가 우리 학교를 방문할 거예요.
bad: The author who's book won the prize will visit our school.
The author which book won the prize will visit our school.
The author whom book won the prize will visit our school.

cz.st: The author ___ book won the prize will visit our school.

items.rule: 소유를 나타내는 관계대명사는 whose예요. who's는 who is의 줄임말이에요.

items.good: Although it was raining, we continued the match.
items.ko: 비가 오고 있었지만 우리는 경기를 계속했어요.
bad: Although it was raining, but we continued the match.
Despite it was raining, we continued the match.
Despite of the rain, we continued the match.

cz.st: ___ it was raining, we continued the match.

items.rule: Although 뒤에는 절이 오고, despite 뒤에는 명사(구)가 와요. 한 문장에 although와 but을 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: I am writing to inquire about the volunteer program.
items.ko: 자원봉사 프로그램에 대해 문의하려고 이 글을 씁니다.
bad: I am writing for inquire about the volunteer program.
I am writing to inquire the volunteer program.
I am writing to inquiring about the volunteer program.

cz.st: I am writing to ___ about the volunteer program.

items.rule: 목적을 나타내는 to 뒤에는 동사원형이 오고, inquire는 about이나 into와 함께 써요.

items.good: The students taking the exam must stay silent.
items.ko: 시험을 치르는 학생들은 조용히 해야 해요.
bad: The students takes the exam must stay silent.
The students taken the exam must stay silent.
The students are taking the exam must stay silent.

cz.st: The students ___ the exam must stay silent.

items.rule: 현재분사구가 명사를 뒤에서 수식해요(= who are taking). 문장에는 동사가 하나(must stay)만 있어야 해요.

items.good: The survey was conducted among 200 students.
items.ko: 그 설문 조사는 학생 200명을 대상으로 실시되었어요.
bad: The survey was conducting among 200 students.
The survey conducted among 200 students.
The survey was conduct among 200 students.

cz.st: The survey was ___ among 200 students.

items.rule: 보고서에서는 수동태(be + p.p.)로 연구 방법을 객관적으로 설명하는 일이 많아요.

items.good: She is an honest person who always tells the truth.
items.ko: 그녀는 항상 진실을 말하는 정직한 사람이에요.
bad: She is a honest person who always tells the truth.
She is an honest person who always tells truth.
She is honest person who always tells the truth.

cz.st: She is ___ honest person who always tells the truth.

items.rule: honest의 h는 소리 나지 않으므로 모음 소리 앞의 an을 써요. 또한 단수 가산명사 앞에는 관사가 필요해요.

items.good: Because of the heavy traffic, we arrived late.
items.ko: 교통 체증 때문에 우리는 늦게 도착했어요.
bad: Because the heavy traffic, we arrived late.
Because of the traffic was heavy, we arrived late.
Because of heavy traffic, arrived we late.

cz.st: ___ the heavy traffic, we arrived late.

items.rule: because of 뒤에는 명사구가, because 뒤에는 절이 와요.

items.good: The report provides a detailed analysis of the data.
items.ko: 그 보고서는 데이터에 대한 상세한 분석을 제공해요.
bad: The report provides a detailed analyze of the data.
The report provides a detailed analytical of the data.
The report provides a detailed analyses of the data.

cz.st: The report provides a detailed ___ of the data.

items.rule: 관사 a와 형용사 뒤에는 단수 명사형(analysis)이 와야 해요. analyses는 복수형이에요.

items.good: The number of students in the club has increased.
items.ko: 동아리 학생 수가 늘었어요.
bad: The number of students in the club have increased.
The number of students in the club are increasing.
The number of student in the club has increased.

cz.st: The number of students in the club ___ increased.

items.rule: the number of는 단수 취급하고, a number of는 복수 취급해요.

items.good: A number of students were absent yesterday.
items.ko: 어제 여러 명의 학생이 결석했어요.
bad: A number of students was absent yesterday.
A number of student were absent yesterday.
A number of students is absent yesterday.

cz.st: A number of students ___ absent yesterday.

items.rule: a number of + 복수명사는 ‘많은 ~’이라는 뜻이고 복수 동사를 써요.

items.good: The more you practice, the better you become.
items.ko: 연습할수록 더 잘하게 돼요.
bad: The more you practice, the more better you become.
More you practice, better you become.
The more you practice, the best you become.

cz.st: The more you practice, the ___ you become.

items.rule: ‘the + 비교급, the + 비교급’은 ‘~할수록 더 …하다’라는 뜻이에요. 이중 비교급(more better)은 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: Not only did she win the prize, but she also broke the record.
items.ko: 그녀는 상을 받았을 뿐만 아니라 기록도 깼어요.
bad: Not only she did win the prize, but she also broke the record.
Not only she won the prize, but she also broke the record.
Not only did she won the prize, but she also broke the record.

cz.st: Not only ___ she win the prize, but she also broke the record.

items.rule: Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 동사가 도치돼요(did + 주어 + 동사원형).

items.good: I look forward to hearing from you.
items.ko: 답장을 기다리겠습니다.
bad: I look forward to hear from you.
I look forward hearing from you.
I look forward for hearing from you.

cz.st: I look forward to ___ from you.

items.rule: look forward to의 to는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사가 와요. 이메일 맺음말에 자주 써요.

items.good: Having finished the essay, she submitted it online.
items.ko: 에세이를 끝낸 뒤 그녀는 온라인으로 제출했어요.
bad: Having finished the essay, it was submitted online.
Having finishing the essay, she submitted it online.
Have finished the essay, she submitted it online.

cz.st: ___ the essay, she submitted it online.

items.rule: 완료 분사구문은 Having + p.p.이고, 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어(she)와 같아야 해요.

items.good: Could you tell me where the post office is?
items.ko: 우체국이 어디 있는지 알려 주시겠어요?
bad: Could you tell me where is the post office?
Could you tell me where does the post office is?
Could you tell me where the post office?

cz.st: Could you tell me where the post office ___?

items.rule: 간접의문문에서는 의문사 뒤의 어순이 ‘주어 + 동사’가 돼요.

items.good: The writer argues that schools should start later.
items.ko: 필자는 학교가 더 늦게 시작해야 한다고 주장해요.
bad: The writer argues that schools should to start later.
The writer argue that schools should start later.
The writer argues that schools should starts later.

cz.st: The writer argues that schools should ___ later.

items.rule: 글쓴이의 주장을 요약할 때는 3인칭 단수 현재형 동사(argues)를 쓰고, should 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요.

items.good: My brother, who lives in Busan, is a nurse.
items.ko: 부산에 사는 내 형(동생)은 간호사예요.
bad: My brother, that lives in Busan, is a nurse.
My brother, which lives in Busan, is a nurse.
My brother, who living in Busan, is a nurse.

cz.st: My brother, ___ lives in Busan, is a nurse.

items.rule: 쉼표로 덧붙이는 관계절에는 that을 쓰지 않아요. 사람이 선행사이고 주격이면 who를 써요.

items.good: They're planning to publish their results next month.
items.ko: 그들은 다음 달에 결과를 발표할 계획이에요.
bad: Their planning to publish they're results next month.
There planning to publish their results next month.
They're planning to publish there results next month.

cz.st: They're planning to publish ___ results next month.

items.rule: they're는 they are, their는 ‘그들의’, there는 ‘거기에’예요.

items.good: It is widely believed that exercise improves memory.
items.ko: 운동이 기억력을 향상시킨다고 널리 믿어져요.
bad: It widely believes that exercise improves memory.
It is widely believe that exercise improves memory.
It is widely believing that exercise improves memory.

cz.st: It is widely ___ that exercise improves memory.

items.rule: ‘It is believed that ~’는 수동태 구문으로 글에서 의견을 객관적으로 전할 때 써요.

items.good: She has been working on her thesis for two years.
items.ko: 그녀는 2년 동안 논문을 쓰고 있어요.
bad: She has been working on her thesis since two years.
She has been work on her thesis for two years.
She is working on her thesis for two years.

cz.st: She has been working on her thesis ___ two years.

items.rule: 기간 앞에는 for를 쓰고, since 뒤에는 시작 시점이 와요. 계속된 동작은 현재완료진행형으로 나타내요.

items.good: Should you need any help, please contact me.
items.ko: 도움이 필요하시면 저에게 연락해 주세요.
bad: If should you need any help, please contact me.
Should you needing any help, please contact me.
Should you to need any help, please contact me.

cz.st: Should you ___ any help, please contact me.

items.rule: Should + 주어 + 동사원형은 If you should need의 도치 형태로 격식 있는 글에 써요. If와 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: What surprised me most was the quality of the data.
items.ko: 나를 가장 놀라게 한 것은 자료의 질이었어요.
bad: That surprised me most was the quality of the data.
What surprised me most were the quality of the data.
Which surprised me most was the quality of the data.

cz.st: ___ surprised me most was the quality of the data.

items.rule: ‘~한 것’을 뜻하는 명사절의 주어는 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what으로 시작해요.

items.good: Rarely do students read the instructions carefully.
items.ko: 학생들은 설명서를 주의 깊게 읽는 일이 거의 없어요.
bad: Rarely students do read the instructions carefully.
Rarely students read the instructions carefully.
Rarely do students reads the instructions carefully.

cz.st: Rarely ___ students read the instructions carefully.

items.rule: rarely 같은 부정 부사가 문두에 오면 주어와 조동사가 도치돼요.

items.good: He must have left his umbrella on the bus.
items.ko: 그는 버스에 우산을 두고 내린 게 틀림없어요.
bad: He must left his umbrella on the bus.
He must has left his umbrella on the bus.
He must have leave his umbrella on the bus.

cz.st: He must have ___ his umbrella on the bus.

items.rule: 과거에 대한 확신 있는 추측은 must have + p.p.로 나타내요.

items.good: She wrote a clear outline so that her readers could follow the argument.
items.ko: 그녀는 독자가 논거를 따라올 수 있도록 명확한 개요를 썼어요.
bad: She wrote a clear outline so that her readers could to follow the argument.
She wrote a clear outline so that her readers could followed the argument.
She wrote a clear outline in order that her readers could following the argument.

cz.st: She wrote a clear outline so that her readers ___ follow the argument.

items.rule: so that + 주어 + could/can + 동사원형은 목적을 나타내요.

items.good: Neither the captain nor the players were ready for the match.
items.ko: 주장도 선수들도 경기 준비가 되어 있지 않았어요.
bad: Neither the captain nor the players was ready for the match.
Neither the captain nor the players is ready for the match.
Neither the captain nor the players be ready for the match.

cz.st: Neither the captain nor the players ___ ready for the match.

items.rule: neither A nor B에서는 동사를 가까운 B(players)에 일치시켜요.

items.good: Each of the essays has a clear title.
items.ko: 에세이마다 분명한 제목이 있어요.
bad: Each of the essays have a clear title.
Each of the essay has a clear title.
Each of the essays having a clear title.

cz.st: Each of the essays ___ a clear title.

items.rule: each of + 복수명사는 단수 취급해요.

items.good: Because the instructions were unclear, many students misunderstood the task.
items.ko: 설명이 불분명해서 많은 학생이 과제를 오해했어요.
bad: Because of the instructions were unclear, many students misunderstood the task.
Because the instructions unclear, many students misunderstood the task.
Because the instructions was unclear, many students misunderstood the task.

cz.st: Because the instructions ___ unclear, many students misunderstood the task.

items.rule: instructions는 복수이므로 were를 써요. Because 뒤에는 완전한 절이 와야 해요.

items.q: Which sentence works best as the topic sentence of a paragraph about the benefits of school gardens?
o: Last spring my class planted tomatoes and peppers beside the gym and watered them every single morning.
School gardens give students practical lessons in science, teamwork, and healthy eating.
Tomatoes, peppers, and lettuce are among the vegetables that grow quickly in warm weather.
Some people think that gardens look pleasant when the weather is warm and sunny outside.
items.why: 주제문은 단락 전체를 아우르는 핵심 생각을 말해야 해요. 나머지는 개별 경험이나 세부 정보예요.

items.q:
Read the paragraph.
(1) Public libraries now offer many services. (2) Some lend tools and musical instruments. (3) Others hold free coding classes. (4) My uncle's bakery sells bread every morning.
Which sentence does not belong?
o: Sentence 1
Sentence 2
Sentence 3
Sentence 4
items.why: (4)는 도서관의 서비스라는 단락의 주제와 관련이 없어요.

items.q: The bakery raised its prices. ___, many loyal customers kept coming.
o: Nevertheless
Therefore
For instance
Similarly
items.why: 가격이 올랐는데도 손님이 계속 왔으므로 역접·양보의 Nevertheless가 알맞아요.

items.q: Many animals adapt to cold climates. ___, the Arctic fox grows a thick white coat in winter.
o: In contrast
As a result
For example
Otherwise
items.why: 북극여우는 앞 문장의 일반 진술에 대한 구체적인 예이므로 For example이 알맞아요.

items.q: Which sentence is most suitable for a formal email asking a principal to extend a deadline?
o: Can you give us more time? Thanks a lot!
I would appreciate it if you could extend the deadline.
Give us a couple more days, okay? We need it.
We think the deadline is too early, honestly, so please change it.
items.why: 격식 있는 이메일에서는 공손한 요청 표현(I would appreciate it if ...)을 써요.

items.q: Which opening sentence states the purpose of an email applying for a volunteer position at an animal shelter?
o: I am writing to apply for the weekend volunteer position at your animal shelter.
Hello, how are you doing today, and did you have a nice weekend with family?
Animals are wonderful creatures, and many people keep them as pets at home.
I saw your shelter once when I was walking to the station with my friends last Saturday afternoon.
items.why: 이메일의 첫 문장은 글을 쓰는 목적을 분명히 밝혀야 해요.

items.q: Which subject line is clearest for an email asking a teacher for a recommendation letter?
o: Hello
A small question about something important for me
Request for a recommendation letter: university application due March 10
Please help me, it is urgent and I have been worried about everything for many days
items.why: 좋은 제목은 요청의 내용과 핵심 정보(기한 등)를 짧게 보여 줘요.

items.q: Which is the strongest thesis statement for an essay about school uniforms?
o: This essay is going to be about school uniforms and what they are.
School uniforms should be optional because they limit self-expression without clearly improving behavior.
Many schools in the world have rules about what students must wear every day.
School uniforms are the clothes that students put on at home before they walk to their classes each morning.
items.why: 논지문은 논쟁의 여지가 있는 입장과 그 이유를 밝혀야 해요. 나머지는 주제 소개이거나 단순한 사실이에요.

items.q: Which sentence is the best concluding sentence for a paragraph arguing that students should learn basic cooking skills?
o: Cooking is something that my family does together in our kitchen.
Therefore, learning to cook prepares students to eat well and live independently.
Some recipes need an oven, while others need only a pan on the stove.
Pasta is easy to make, and many students already like eating it at lunch with their friends in the cafeteria.
items.why: 맺음 문장은 앞에서 말한 주장을 요약하고 의미를 마무리해야 해요.

items.q:
Read the passage.
A city planted trees along its busiest streets. The trees shaded the sidewalks and lowered the temperature on hot days. Residents also said the streets felt calmer and more pleasant.
Which sentence is the best summary?
o: Tree planting made a city's streets cooler and more pleasant.
A city has many busy streets with sidewalks on both sides.
Residents of a city complained about the hot weather on busy days.
Trees need shade and calm streets in order to grow in a city.
items.why: 요약은 글의 핵심(나무 심기의 효과)만 짧게 담아야 해요.

items.q: Which sentence best paraphrases “Despite her limited experience, she handled the project skillfully”?
o: Because she had little experience, she handled the project badly.
Although she had little experience, she managed the project well.
She had a lot of experience, so she managed the project well.
She handled the project well, so she needed to gain experience.
items.why: Despite는 양보를 나타내므로 Although 절로 바꿀 수 있어요. 나머지는 의미가 달라요.

items.q: Which sentence combines “The museum was crowded. We stayed for three hours.” without changing the meaning?
o: Because we stayed for three hours, the museum was crowded.
The museum was crowded, so we left after a short time.
Although the museum was crowded, we stayed for three hours.
The museum was crowded after we stayed there for three hours.
items.why: 붐볐지만 오래 머물렀다는 대조 관계이므로 Although로 연결해요.

items.q: Which revision removes the redundancy from “The reason is because the road was closed”?
o: The reason is that the road was closed.
The reason is because of the road closed.
The reason because the road was closed is.
Because is the reason the road was closed.
items.why: ‘The reason is because’는 의미가 중복돼요. ‘The reason is that ...’으로 고쳐요.

items.q: Which revision fixes the unclear pronoun in “When Sora met Eun, she was carrying a heavy bag”?
o: Sora met Eun when she was carrying a heavy bag.
When Sora met Eun, Sora was carrying a heavy bag.
When the two girls met, she was carrying a heavy bag.
When Sora met Eun, she herself was carrying it.
items.why: she가 누구를 가리키는지 모호하므로 이름을 다시 써서 분명하게 해요. 나머지는 여전히 모호하거나 ‘it’의 지시 대상이 없어요.

items.q: Complete the list in parallel form: “The course will teach students to plan an essay, to support an argument, and ___.”
o: revising of drafts
to revise a draft
a draft revision
when they revise
items.why: 나열된 항목은 모두 to + 동사원형 형태로 맞추어야 해요.

items.q: Which sentence is most appropriately cautious for an academic claim based on a small survey?
o: The results prove that sleep always decides test scores.
Everyone knows that students who sleep well never fail.
The results suggest that sleep may influence test scores.
It is a fact that sleep is the only cause of high grades.
items.why: 작은 조사에서 나온 결과는 suggest, may 같은 완곡한 표현으로 조심스럽게 말해야 해요.

items.q: Which bullet point is best for the “Experience” section of a résumé?
o: I was the person who did some recycling stuff at school.
Organized a school recycling campaign that collected 300 kilograms of paper.
Recycling is good for nature and I think everybody should do it at home and at school.
Helped with various things related to the environment in several ways.
items.why: 이력서에서는 동사로 시작해 구체적인 행동과 수치로 성과를 보여 줘요.

items.q: Which sentence is the best closing for a cover letter?
o: I look forward to the opportunity to discuss my application further.
Please remember that I am the best person you will ever interview this year.
That is all I have to say about myself at the moment, thanks.
Call me whenever you want, and we can decide everything quickly.
items.why: 자기소개서의 끝맺음은 공손하고 전문적인 어조로 면접 기회를 바라는 표현이 알맞아요.

items.q: Which verb best completes “The report ___ a strong case for renewable energy”?
o: does
gets
makes
holds
items.why: make a case for는 ‘~에 대한 주장을 펼치다’라는 연어(collocation)예요.

items.q: Which word best completes “The data ___ that cities with more trees are cooler in summer”?
o: pretend
indicate
apologize
borrow
items.why: 데이터가 ‘보여 주다’는 indicate, show, suggest 등을 써요. 나머지는 의미가 맞지 않아요.

items.q: Which sentence sounds most polite when declining an invitation in a letter?
o: No, I can't come. I'm busy.
Thank you for inviting me, but I am afraid I cannot attend.
I won't be there, so don't wait for me at all.
Why would you invite me to that kind of boring party in the first place?
items.why: 초대를 정중히 거절할 때는 감사 표현과 완곡한 표현(I am afraid)을 써요.

items.q: Which word is the most formal replacement for “get” in “You will get a certificate after the course”?
o: grab
receive
catch
retrieve
items.why: 격식 있는 글에서 get(받다)은 receive로 바꿔 써요.

items.q: Which detail best supports the topic sentence “Regular exercise improves concentration”?
o: In one study, students who walked for twenty minutes before class scored higher on attention tests.
Many gyms offer special discounts to students during the summer holidays every year in most large cities across the country.
Running shoes are made with a soft material that makes them comfortable to wear.
Some people prefer to exercise in the morning, while others prefer the evening.
items.why: 주제문을 뒷받침하려면 운동과 집중력의 관계를 보여 주는 구체적인 증거가 필요해요.

items.q:
Put the sentences in order.
A. Finally, serve the rice while it is still warm.
B. To begin, measure the rice and the water.
C. Next, boil the water and add the rice.
D. Cook it on low heat for fifteen minutes.
o: B - C - D - A
C - B - D - A
B - D - C - A
B - C - A - D
items.why: 순서 표지어(To begin, Next, Finally)와 요리 과정의 논리를 따르면 B-C-D-A예요.

items.q: Which sentence reports the question “Where is the library?” correctly?
o: She asked where was the library.
She asked where the library was.
She asked that where the library was.
She asked where did the library be.
items.why: 간접화법에서는 의문사 뒤에 ‘주어 + 동사’ 순서를 쓰고 시제를 한 단계 과거로 바꿔요.

items.q: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
o: Although the bus was late; we walked to school.
We walked to school; because the bus was late.
The bus was late; we walked to school instead.
The bus was late; walked to school instead.
items.why: 세미콜론은 서로 밀접한 두 개의 독립된 문장을 연결해요.

items.q: Which of the following is a complete sentence?
o: The students who joined the club every Friday.
Because the students joined the club on Friday.
Meeting every Friday in the old gym after the lessons end.
The students who joined the club met every Friday.
items.why: 주어와 본동사(met)가 있고 의미가 완결된 문장만 완전한 문장이에요.

items.q: Which option corrects the run-on sentence “The film was long we enjoyed it”?
o: The film was long, we enjoyed it.
The film was long and, we enjoyed it.
The film was long, but we enjoyed it.
The film was long, so but we enjoyed it.
items.why: 두 절은 접속사(but)와 쉼표로 연결해야 해요. 쉼표만 쓰면 콤마 스플라이스예요.

items.q: Which phrase best fills the blank? “Many teenagers sleep less than eight hours a night. ___ can harm their health and their grades.”
o: Those shortage of sleep
These shortage of sleep
That shortages of sleep
This shortage of sleep
items.why: 앞 내용을 가리키는 단수 명사구는 This shortage of sleep이에요. 단수 명사와 수가 일치해야 해요.

items.q: A student wants to persuade the school board to lengthen the lunch break. Which type of writing fits best?
o: an opinion letter to the board
a recipe for a school lunch
a weather report for the week
a diary entry about last weekend
items.why: 설득이 목적이면 근거를 들어 주장하는 의견문(편지)이 알맞아요.

items.q: Which sentence would make the most effective opening for an essay about plastic waste in the ocean?
o: In this essay, I will write about plastic waste in the ocean.
Every day, plastic drifts into the sea, where fish and birds often mistake it for food.
Plastic is a material that is made in large factories and used in a great many different products.
I do not like plastic very much, and I try not to use it.
items.why: 좋은 도입은 독자의 관심을 끌며 주제를 구체적인 장면으로 소개해요.

items.q: Which action shows respect for writing ethics when you use another writer's idea?
o: Copy the paragraph and delete the author's name
Change a few words and hide the original source
Use it freely because it was found on the internet
Put it in your own words and credit the author
items.why: 다른 사람의 생각은 자기 말로 바꾸어 쓰고 출처를 밝혀야 해요.

items.q: Which of these is plagiarism?
o: Quoting one sentence in quotation marks and naming the author of the book
Submitting an essay that a friend wrote and calling it your own
Summarizing an article and listing it in your bibliography
Using a dictionary to check the spelling of a difficult word
items.why: 남이 쓴 글을 자기 것처럼 제출하는 것이 표절이에요.

items.q: Which revision best improves the vague sentence “The movie was good”?
o: The movie was good in many good ways, and I liked it.
The movie was really, really good, I think, and I enjoyed it.
The movie's quick plot and warm humor kept the audience laughing.
The movie was good, and it was a movie that many people watched in the city.
items.why: 막연한 표현(good)은 구체적인 세부 내용으로 바꾸면 더 생생해져요.

items.q: Which sentence is in the active voice and keeps the meaning of “The window was broken by the ball”?
o: The ball broke the window.
The window broke the ball.
The window was broken by a ball.
The ball was broken by the window.
items.why: 능동태는 행위자(the ball)가 주어가 돼요. 나머지는 수동태이거나 의미가 달라요.

items.q: A bar graph shows the percentage of students who bike to school: 12% in 2015, 15% in 2020, and 30% in 2024. Which sentence describes it accurately?
o: Bike use fell after 2020.
The biggest increase came between 2015 and 2020.
The largest rise happened between 2020 and 2024, when use doubled.
Bike use stayed about the same over the three years that the graph covers.
items.why: 2020년 15%에서 2024년 30%로 두 배가 되어 가장 크게 늘었어요.

items.q: Which sentence is the best ending for a complaint email about a damaged item?
o: I would be grateful if you could replace the item or refund my payment.
I will never shop at your store again and I will tell everyone I know about this.
Anyway, the box was also a little dirty, but that is not important.
I hope you have a nice day, and I am sorry for writing so much.
items.why: 불만 이메일은 원하는 해결책을 정중하지만 분명하게 요구하며 끝맺어요.

items.q: Which sentence uses sensory detail most effectively?
o: The kitchen was nice and I liked being in it at that time.
The kitchen smelled of toasted sesame and warm bread.
There were many things in the kitchen when we arrived there.
The kitchen was a place where people usually prepared meals.
items.why: 감각적 묘사는 냄새, 소리, 촉감 등을 구체적으로 나타내 장면을 생생하게 해요.

items.q: Which sentence would NOT fit in an essay arguing that schools should start later?
o: Teenagers tend to fall asleep later at night than younger children.
Tired students often find it hard to pay attention in the first lesson.
Pizza is a popular lunch dish in many countries around the world.
A later start could give students more time to eat breakfast at home.
items.why: 피자에 관한 문장은 등교 시간 주장과 관련이 없어요.

items.q: What is the main purpose of the editing stage in the writing process?
o: Collecting ideas before writing the first line
Checking and correcting grammar, spelling, and punctuation
Choosing a topic together with other classmates and the teacher
Deciding the order in which the paragraphs will appear
items.why: 편집 단계에서는 문법, 철자, 문장 부호의 오류를 점검하고 고쳐요.

items.q: Which title is best for a news article about a school that reduced food waste by sorting leftovers?
o: A Long and Happy Day at Our Local Middle School
Why I Really Like Eating Lunch with My Friends
Food Is Good for You
School Cuts Food Waste by Sorting Leftovers
items.why: 기사 제목은 핵심 사건을 간결하고 구체적으로 알려 줘요.

items.q: Which sentence best connects a paragraph about the advantages of online classes to one about their drawbacks?
o: For example, online classes use computers and the internet.
In conclusion, online classes are good for every student.
Despite these advantages, online learning also presents several challenges.
Therefore, all of the drawbacks of online classes are really advantages.
items.why: 장점에서 단점으로 넘어갈 때는 대조를 나타내는 연결 문장(Despite ...)이 알맞아요.

items.q: Which word best completes “The writer's argument is persuasive ___ she supports each claim with evidence”?
o: although
unless
because
until
items.why: 근거로 주장을 뒷받침하기 때문에 설득력이 있다는 인과 관계이므로 because가 알맞아요.

items.title: Why Handwriting Still Matters
items.text: Many schools now give every student a tablet, and some teachers wonder whether pens and notebooks are becoming obsolete. I believe handwriting still deserves a place in the classroom. When we write by hand, we usually cannot copy every word a teacher says, so we must decide what is important and put it in our own words. That process helps ideas stay in our memory. Of course, typing has clear advantages: it is faster, and it makes editing easy. However, speed is not always the goal of learning. A student who types a whole lecture may end up with a perfect record but little understanding. For this reason, I suggest that schools use both methods, asking students to take notes by hand and to type their final drafts.

qs.q: What is the writer's main point?
o: Tablets are harmful and should be removed from every classroom immediately.
Typing is too slow to be useful for students who take notes in class.
Handwriting aids learning, so schools should combine it with typing.
Teachers should stop asking students to edit and correct their drafts.
qs.why: 필자는 손글씨의 학습 효과를 말하며 두 방법을 함께 쓰자고 제안해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, why does writing by hand help memory?
o: Pens make students feel calmer during long lectures.
Students must pick key ideas and put them in their own words.
Students can copy the lecture word for word and read it later.
Notebooks are lighter and easier to carry around than tablets.
qs.why: 손으로 쓰면 모든 말을 받아 적을 수 없어 중요한 것을 골라 자기 말로 바꾸게 돼요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention that typing is faster?
o: To prove that handwriting is actually the quicker method
To admit a point in favor of the opposing view
To explain why tablets are cheaper for most schools
To show that teachers dislike the use of notebooks
qs.why: 반대 입장의 장점을 인정한 뒤 However로 자신의 주장을 이어 가요.

qs.q: The word “obsolete” in the first sentence is closest in meaning to
o: outdated
fragile
valuable
illegal
qs.why: obsolete는 ‘더 이상 쓰이지 않는, 구식의’라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer imply about a student who types a whole lecture?
o: The student will always earn lower scores than classmates.
The student probably cannot read his own handwriting.
The student is likely to finish editing sooner than others.
The student may not have thought deeply about the content.
qs.why: ‘완벽한 기록이지만 이해는 적을 수 있다’는 말에서 내용을 깊이 처리하지 않았음을 추론할 수 있어요.

items.title: Request to Use Room 204
items.text:
Subject: Request to use Room 204 for the Photography Club
Dear Mr. Han,
I am writing on behalf of the Photography Club to ask whether we may use Room 204 on Thursday afternoons from 4:00 to 5:30 during the autumn term. Our club has grown from six to fifteen members this year, and the school library, where we usually meet, no longer has enough space for our printing equipment. Room 204 has large tables and plenty of power outlets, which would suit our activities well. We promise to leave the room clean and to lock the door after each meeting. I would appreciate a reply by next Friday so that we can inform our members. Thank you for considering our request.
Sincerely,
Yuna Seo
Club President

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this email?
o: To ask permission to hold club meetings in a different room
To invite the teacher to see an exhibition of club photographs
To complain that the library is too noisy for printing work
To announce that the club has grown to fifteen members
qs.why: 필자는 동아리 모임을 위해 Room 204를 쓸 수 있는지 허락을 구하고 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the club want to leave the library?
o: The library closes before the Thursday meetings start.
Members would like larger windows to take better pictures.
There is not enough space there for their printing equipment.
The librarian does not allow members to use cameras inside the reading area.
qs.why: 도서관에는 인쇄 장비를 둘 공간이 부족하다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the email, the phrase “on behalf of” means
o: in spite of
representing
in front of
in exchange for
qs.why: on behalf of는 ‘~을 대표하여’라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which best describes the tone of the email?
o: Polite and formal
Casual and joking
Angry and demanding
Shy and uncertain
qs.why: I would appreciate, Thank you for considering 등 공손하고 격식 있는 표현을 써요.

qs.q: Why does Yuna ask for a reply by next Friday?
o: The autumn term will end on that day.
She needs to tell the club members the result.
Mr. Han will be away from school afterward.
The printing equipment must be bought by then.
qs.why: 회원들에게 알려 주어야 하므로 그때까지 답장이 필요하다고 했어요.

items.title: Libraries in the Digital Age
items.text: People once pictured a library as a quiet room full of shelves and a strict librarian. Today, many libraries look quite different. Alongside books, they lend e-readers, musical instruments, and even garden tools. Some offer free classes in coding or job-interview skills, while others provide meeting rooms where neighbors can discuss local issues. These changes do not mean that books have lost their importance; rather, libraries have expanded their mission from storing information to helping people use it. As a result, a library can serve a retired teacher looking for a novel, a teenager preparing for exams, and a newcomer learning the local language, all under one roof. Critics worry that this broad approach may weaken the focus on reading, but supporters respond that the activities draw new visitors who often end up borrowing books too.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How libraries have widened the services they offer
Why people no longer borrow printed books from libraries
How to prepare for a job interview at a library
Which musical instruments are lent by libraries
qs.why: 도서관이 책 보관에서 정보 활용을 돕는 곳으로 역할을 넓혔다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Which service is NOT mentioned in the passage?
o: Lending garden tools
Offering coding classes
Providing meeting rooms
Selling cooked meals
qs.why: 음식을 판매한다는 언급은 없어요.

qs.q: What does “this broad approach” refer to?
o: Storing books on many shelves
Offering many kinds of activities and services
Teaching newcomers the local language and nothing else
Making libraries quiet and strict places
qs.why: 앞에서 설명한 다양한 서비스와 활동을 가리켜요.

qs.q: How do supporters answer the critics' worry?
o: By promising to buy many new novels for the main collection
By saying that reading is no longer important to most visitors
By noting that visitors drawn by activities often borrow books too
By closing the meeting rooms during the busy exam season each year
qs.why: 활동 덕분에 온 사람들이 책도 빌리게 된다고 반박해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the writer's view of the changes?
o: The writer sees them as natural and useful.
The writer believes libraries should return to the past.
The writer thinks books will soon disappear completely.
The writer is unsure whether anyone visits libraries.
qs.why: 변화를 설명하며 비판에 대한 반론도 소개하는 중립적이면서 긍정적인 어조예요.

items.title: My Grandmother's Notebook
items.text: After my grandmother passed away, my mother handed me a small green notebook that I had never seen before. I expected recipes, since Grandma had cooked for half the village, and in a way I was right. But between the lists of ingredients she had written short notes: “Too much salt; Minho laughed.” “Rain today, soup for the neighbors.” I sat on the floor for an hour, reading the sentences that were not really about food at all. They were about people. At first I felt a heavy sadness, but slowly it was replaced by something warmer, as if she were sitting beside me, stirring a pot. That evening I opened the notebook to a blank page and began my own list. My first entry was simple: “Burnt rice. Mom pretended it was delicious.”

qs.q: What did the narrator find between the lists of ingredients?
o: Photographs of neighbors from the village
Short notes about people and daily moments
Instructions for repairing a kitchen pot
Letters addressed to the narrator's mother
qs.why: 재료 목록 사이에 사람들과 일상에 관한 짧은 메모가 있었어요.

qs.q: How did the narrator's feelings change?
o: From curiosity to bitter disappointment and regret
From sadness to a warmer, comforted feeling
From anger to embarrassment
From boredom to fear
qs.why: 무거운 슬픔이 점차 따뜻한 기분으로 바뀌었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does “in a way I was right” suggest?
o: The notebook was full of recipes only.
The notebook was not written by Grandma.
The narrator guessed the topic of the notebook incorrectly.
The notebook did contain food, but also much more.
qs.why: 요리 관련 내용이 있었지만 그것이 전부는 아니었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does the narrator begin a notebook of their own?
o: To record people and moments that matter, as Grandma did
To collect all of Grandma's recipes in one place before they are forgotten
To practise cooking before the next family dinner
To give the notebook back to their mother
qs.why: 할머니처럼 소중한 사람과 순간을 기록하려는 마음이 드러나요.

qs.q: What is the tone of the first entry, “Burnt rice. Mom pretended it was delicious”?
o: Bitter and resentful toward her mother
Cold and strictly formal throughout
Affectionate and lightly humorous
Serious and deeply fearful about it
qs.why: 엄마의 배려를 떠올리며 다정하고 가볍게 웃음 짓는 어조예요.

items.title: A Personal Statement
items.text: Ever since I joined the school newspaper in my first year, I have been fascinated by the way a few carefully chosen words can change what people think. My first article, about long queues in the cafeteria, led the school to add a second serving line, and that small victory taught me that writing can solve real problems. Since then, I have interviewed teachers, edited the weekly column, and trained younger members. These experiences have made me more patient and more willing to listen to opinions that differ from mine. I hope to study journalism at university, where I want to learn how to check facts rigorously and report responsibly. I believe my curiosity, together with my experience of working under deadlines, will allow me to contribute to your program.

qs.q: What kind of text is this most likely to be?
o: Part of a college application essay
A news report about a school cafeteria
A letter complaining about a newspaper
A review of a book about journalism
qs.why: 자신의 경험과 진학 목표를 밝히며 프로그램에 기여하겠다고 해 지원서 글임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What did the writer's first article lead to?
o: The creation of a weekly column
A change in how the cafeteria served students
The writer's selection as editor-in-chief
A new rule about the length of school articles
qs.why: 급식실에 배식 줄이 하나 더 생겼다고 했어요.

qs.q: According to the writer, how have the experiences changed the writer?
o: They have made the writer faster at typing.
They have made the writer afraid of deadlines.
They have made the writer more open to different opinions.
They have made the writer more interested in cooking and gardening.
qs.why: 더 인내심이 생기고 다른 의견을 기꺼이 듣게 되었다고 했어요.

qs.q: The word “rigorously” in the passage is closest in meaning to
o: carelessly
with great care
quickly and loudly
secretly
qs.why: rigorously는 ‘엄격하고 철저하게’라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How are the first article and the writer's later attitude related?
o: The first success showed the writer that writing can solve real problems.
The first failure convinced the writer to quit the newspaper and play sports instead.
The first complaint made the writer dislike interviewing teachers and other adults at school.
The first prize gave the writer enough money to attend university.
qs.why: 작은 성공이 글쓰기가 실제 문제를 해결할 수 있다는 깨달음으로 이어졌어요.

items.title: Rooftop Garden Opens
items.text: A rooftop garden opened at Harbor Middle School on Monday, giving students a new place to grow vegetables and study science. The project began two years ago, when a group of eighth graders asked the principal whether the unused roof could serve a purpose. After months of planning and a fundraising sale of handmade cards, the school raised enough money to build twelve raised beds and a small rainwater tank. Science teacher Ms. Park said that students will measure plant growth every week and record the results in a shared notebook. Part of the harvest will be used in the school kitchen, and the rest will be donated to a local food bank. “We wanted something that would teach responsibility and also help others,” said Hana, one of the original organizers. The garden will be open to families on the first Saturday of every month.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the article?
o: A school has opened a rooftop garden for learning and sharing.
A principal has banned students from using the school roof for sports.
Eighth graders have won a science competition in the city.
A food bank has started selling vegetables to schools.
qs.why: 옥상 정원의 개장과 그 목적을 알리는 기사예요.

qs.q: How did the school pay for the garden?
o: With a grant from the local food bank
With money from a sale of handmade cards
With a donation from the science teacher
With fees paid by families each month
qs.why: 손수 만든 카드를 판 모금 행사로 비용을 마련했어요.

qs.q: What will happen to the vegetables that are not used in the school kitchen?
o: They will be sold at a market on Saturdays.
They will be given to a local food bank.
They will be taken home by the eighth graders.
They will be kept for next year's science class.
qs.why: 나머지는 지역 푸드뱅크에 기부된다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Hana?
o: She was involved in starting the project.
She teaches the science class at the school.
She is the principal of the school.
She works at the local food bank.
qs.why: 원래 기획자 중 한 명이라고 소개돼 프로젝트를 시작한 학생임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which statement is true according to the article?
o: The garden is open to families every Saturday throughout the whole year.
The garden has twelve raised beds and a small rainwater tank.
Students will record plant growth once a year in a shared school notebook.
The project started only last month.
qs.why: 열두 개의 화단과 작은 빗물 탱크를 만들었다고 했어요.

items.title: Phones at Lunch
items.text: Should students be allowed to use their phones during lunch? Supporters say that lunchtime is free time, and checking messages or listening to music helps students relax. They add that a ban would be difficult to enforce, since teachers cannot watch every table. Opponents, however, point out that many students spend the whole break looking at a screen instead of talking to friends. In their view, a lunchroom full of silent faces defeats the purpose of a shared meal. A reasonable compromise might be to set aside certain tables as phone-free zones. This would respect the freedom of those who want to relax with their devices while giving others a chance to enjoy real conversation. Whatever the school decides, the rule should be explained clearly, so that students understand the reasons behind it rather than simply obeying orders.

qs.q: What is the writer's position on the issue?
o: The writer fully supports a complete ban on phones throughout the school day.
The writer suggests a compromise that considers both sides.
The writer believes teachers should watch every table.
The writer thinks lunch should be shorter for everyone.
qs.why: 양쪽 입장을 소개한 뒤 일부 구역만 휴대폰 금지로 하는 절충안을 제안해요.

qs.q: Which argument do supporters of phone use give?
o: Phones are useful for taking notes during lunch.
Screens make it easier for students to talk to friends.
A ban would save the school money on equipment.
Lunchtime is free time, and phones help students relax.
qs.why: 점심시간은 자유 시간이고 휴대폰이 긴장을 풀어 준다는 것이 찬성 측 논거예요.

qs.q: What does “This” refer to in “This would respect the freedom of those who want to relax with their devices”?
o: Banning phones from the whole lunchroom
Explaining the new rule to all students
Setting aside some tables as phone-free zones
Letting everyone use phones at every table
qs.why: This는 바로 앞 문장의 절충안, 즉 일부 테이블을 휴대폰 금지 구역으로 정하는 것을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What does the phrase “a shared meal” suggest about the opponents' view?
o: Meals are best eaten quickly and alone.
Lunch should be a time for people to interact.
Food should be served by the students themselves.
Everyone should eat the same dishes at lunch.
qs.why: 함께 먹는 식사의 목적은 대화와 교류라는 의미를 담고 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say the rule should be explained clearly?
o: So that students understand the reasons instead of just obeying
So that teachers have much less work to do during the long lunch break
So that parents can send messages during lunch
So that students stop using phones at home
qs.why: 학생들이 이유를 이해하고 규칙을 받아들이게 하기 위해서예요.

items.title: Green Roofs
items.text: In crowded cities, rooftops are usually bare surfaces of concrete or tar that soak up the summer sun. In recent years, however, more buildings have been covered with soil and plants, forming what are known as green roofs. The plants shade the surface beneath them and release water vapor, which cools the surrounding air. In addition, the soil absorbs rainwater, so less of it rushes into the drains during heavy storms. Building owners also benefit, because the layer of plants acts like a blanket, keeping rooms warmer in winter and cooler in summer, which lowers energy bills. Still, green roofs are not without drawbacks. They are heavier than ordinary roofs, so the building must be strong enough to support them, and they need regular care. For these reasons, many experts recommend them for new buildings rather than for old ones.

qs.q: How is the passage organized?
o: Advantages, then drawbacks, then a recommendation
A personal story followed by a list of rules
A history of roofs from ancient times to the modern day
Two opinions followed by the writer's complaint
qs.why: 장점, 단점, 전문가의 권고 순으로 전개돼요.

qs.q: Why does less rainwater rush into the drains during storms?
o: Plants release water vapor into the drains.
Roofs of concrete and tar hold rain for a long time.
The soil of a green roof absorbs part of the water.
Building owners cover the drains in heavy weather.
qs.why: 흙이 빗물을 흡수해 배수구로 흘러드는 양이 줄어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the layer of plants “acts like a blanket” means that it
o: makes the building look soft and warm
covers the building to protect it from rain
hides ugly surfaces from people on the street
keeps the temperature inside more stable
qs.why: 담요처럼 겨울에는 따뜻하게, 여름에는 시원하게 해 주는 단열 효과를 비유한 거예요.

qs.q: Which word signals a change from advantages to disadvantages?
o: In addition
Still
Also
As
qs.why: Still은 앞의 장점과 대조되는 단점을 소개할 때 써요.

qs.q: Why do many experts recommend green roofs for new buildings?
o: Old buildings do not have any roofs at all.
New buildings need fewer plants than old ones do, so they cost less.
New buildings can be designed to carry the extra weight.
Green roofs are cheaper to remove from new buildings.
qs.why: 녹화 지붕은 무거워서 건물이 이를 지탱하도록 설계되어야 하기 때문이에요.
